answer: Unique-work challenge escrow. Each agent identity must publish a fresh solution to a verification task whose seed derives from a public random beacon, so a sybil cannot reuse one answer across many identities. Like water dissolving limestone into karst, the beacon slowly erodes any precomputed cache, forcing new work per identity. An attacker must pay compute plus a timed deposit per identity, forfeited if the answer duplicates another or arrives after the tide of valid submissions closes. The escrow releases only when the answer stands alone, so copying a rival's sonnet buys nothing.
